title: Amend the board: batched toast wording, repo-named decision toasts, an honest tool result and a narrow-terminal band (seq 182)
description: opum-doc ruling seq 182 amends the three board changes that just landed on dev (QCLI-440/441/442): the batched alert toast must point at the dashboard tool instead of the retired /quest command; the two decision toasts must name the repository because a decision id is minted per workspace (two trackers can both hold DEC-3); and the dashboard tool result must report what actually happened instead of claiming a pane the surface kept undrawn. Because an unasked $.ui.open is placed only from 144 terminal columns, a narrow terminal also needs a reachable path: a one-line band above the prompt with an Open button whose press is the person asking. The band-press seating behaviour below 144 columns is to be measured, not assumed.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The batched alert toast line ends with the literal Open the board: /quest dashboard, and hooks/quest.ts holds no remaining reference to a bare /quest command.

The two decision toasts print the repository: <repo> <id> needs a decision: <title> and <repo> <id> decided: <status>; a test drives the same decision id from two workspaces and the two toasts are distinguishable.

The dashboard tool result says Opened the Quest board only when the engine record from $.ui.panes() reports the board pane placed and shown; when the pane is waiting undrawn the result instead says the board is waiting for a terminal at least 144 columns wide.

While the board pane is waiting undrawn, the mod draws a one-line band above the prompt reading Quest board ready with a Button labelled Open whose hotkey is o; pressing it opens the pane, and the band stops drawing once the pane is placed.

The band-press seating question is answered with evidence: either a test shows the pane placed after a band press at a viewport under 144 columns, or the task note and the report state with the measurement that it does not seat.

plan: 1. Change batchLine and the decision toasts in hooks/quest.ts, and their tests in tests/board.test.tsx.
2. Make the dashboard tool result honest: read $.ui.panes() after the open and report placed/shown truthfully.
3. Add the AbovePrompt band with an Open button and measure whether its press seats the pane below 144 columns.
4. Prove every changed test fails pre-change; run every gate.
implementationNotes:
seq 182 landed with tests. Commit da10cc1 on fix/QCLI-444-seq182-board. Four changes: the batched line now ends with the literal Open the board: /quest dashboard; both decision toasts print <repo> <id>; the dashboard tool result is read from $.ui.panes() and requires the pane to be both placed and shown, saying the board waits for a terminal at least 144 columns wide otherwise; and a one-line band above the prompt (Text Quest board ready, Button Open at hotkey o) is drawn only while the pane waits undrawn, opening it with focus (the person asking) and invalidating ui.render so the band comes down.

Band-press seating, measured live at 100 columns on 2026-10-02 (AC4): the unasked open at session.start returned {"isPlaced":false,"reason":"unasked below 144 columns (100 now): placed when the person opens it, or when the terminal is widened to 144 columns"}; pressing the band Button then returned {"opened":{"isPlaced":true},"after":[{"id":"seat-probe2","title":"Seat probe 2","isShown":true,"isFocused":false,"isPlaced":true}]}. So a band press DOES seat the pane below 144 columns. The raw probe log is qcli444-probe-report.txt in the worktree, deliberately uncommitted scratch; the mod suite asserts the mod-side half of that open, that the press carries focus.

Evidence: mod suite 42 tests pass, 0 fail, 33 of them the board in tests/board.test.tsx, run by npm run test:mod (claude plugin test; the runner reports NOT TYPECHECKED, no declaration for Claude Code 2.1.288 on this machine). Repository suite npm test: 1081 pass, 1 fail, the failure being test/qcli411-bun-declare-binding.test.ts, which fails because this machine runs bun 1.3.14 while package.json pins 1.4.2 -- the check working, not this change. typecheck, lint, format:check and layer:check all exit 0.

Red evidence: eight mutations of the hooks, each reverted after its run, reddening only the predicted tests: band draws nothing -> 1 of 42; band drops the isPlaced guard -> 2 (both band tests, since the withdraw assertion is in the first); press drops focus -> 1; press drops the invalidate -> 1; boardIsShown drops isShown -> 1; boardIsShown always true -> 1; batchLine reverted -> 2 (the batched toast and the line unit test); decision toasts drop the repo -> 4 (waiting decision, same-id-two-workspaces, batched toast, toast unit).
